findings.text: follow-on: the reviewed manifest's baseline_suite.command, echoed on logs/baseline-d934afc8c.log's own command line, carries a literal <base> placeholder in place of the scratch tree path, and the base log's header names neither the module under test as imported (module.__file__) nor the resolved working directory; the base arm therefore cannot be replayed or its resolution confirmed from the record alone, though its revision d934afc8c and result 113 passed EXIT=0 are stated.

follow-on: the answer verb imports the module-private reckon.mcp._stale_plan_review across the package boundary, so the stale-review message's single owner is reached through a private name; if two surfaces are meant to share it, making it public (or hoisting it beside the coverage predicate) would state that contract rather than imply it.

item_verdicts.goal: The node goal is met: reckon/cli.py:2619 calls plan_review.store_delivered_reviews(project, plan_slug) before the read at reckon/cli.py:2621, and both reckon/cli.py:2621 and reckon/mcp.py:4351 resolve the plan file through _store._resolve_html_file and pass it to read_plan_review, so answering a finding no longer depends on a prior build having stored the delivery and a plan covered section by section reads as reviewed on both surfaces.

item_verdicts.write_paths: git diff --stat d934afc8c..39ee1c083 is four files - reckon/cli.py, reckon/mcp.py, tests/test_the_surfaces_pass_the_plan.py and docs/evidence/fragments/a-plan-is-reviewed-before-it-is-built/the-surfaces-pass-the-plan.html - 395 insertions against nine deletions, every one inside the node's declared write paths with no plan meta line and no shared index touched.

justifications.durability: both halves are now guarded where an earlier review found the plan-content half unguarded - removing store_delivered_reviews reddens the delivery test and dropping plan= from both callers reddens the two coverage tests and the absent-covering test (I reproduced 3 failed 1 passed), on a self-contained two-review fixture with pinned mtimes; the deduction is the untested mcp path where the resolver raises and the view returns a crew_error rather than the stale-review note.
justifications.evidence: strong - the gate is recorded (117 passed EXIT=0, logs/gate-ac592068.log) with a real base arm this time (113 passed EXIT=0, logs/baseline-d934afc8c.log), I reproduced the new module (4 passed) and both negative controls (1 failed 2 passed; 3 failed 1 passed, each ending EXIT=1), and public_definitions is 1481 at both revisions; the deduction is that the base arm's command carries a literal <base> placeholder and its header names neither the module under test as imported nor the resolved working directory, so the base arm is not fully replayable from the record.
justifications.fit: the callers reuse the existing _resolve_html_file resolver the plan editor and promotion already use, the stale message is composed once, and the tests are named by behaviour with no plan, ticket or version label; the deduction is that the answer verb reaches the module-private reckon.mcp._stale_plan_review across the package boundary, so a private name is now a cross-package dependency.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/cli.py:2619 stores the delivery before the read at reckon/cli.py:2621, and both it and reckon/mcp.py:4351 select the review through the plan's content, which is the node goal stated exactly.
justifications.reuse: the change extends the existing store step (store_delivered_reviews), reader (read_plan_review) and resolver (_resolve_html_file) rather than forking any, and read_plan_review keeps its name and its single owner of the coverage choice.
